questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical mastery of TLS handling in Kubernetes Pods, in-place certificate reload without downtime, and config-driven rollout control. It combines InitContainers, sidecars, ConfigMaps, and PodDisruptionBudgets—core CKAD patterns.

## Key Concepts
- TLS certificate management via Secrets and mounted volumes
- InitContainer bootstrap logic for preparing volume mounts
- Sidecar pattern for in-process TLS reload without pod restarts
- ConfigMap-driven feature flags with rolling update triggers
- Kubernetes probes, preStop lifecycle hooks, resource governance, and PodDisruptionBudget for high availability

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-api
  namespace: ssl
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secure-api
      annotations:
        checksum/config: $(kubectl get configmap rotation-config -n ssl -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.checksum}')
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: tls-init
          image: busybox
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'mkdir -p /tls && chmod 777 /tls']
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tls-certs
              mountPath: /tls
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: your-api-image:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8443
              name: https
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8443
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 8443
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ['sh', '-c', 'sleep 10']
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: "128Mi"
              cpu: "100m"
            limits:
              memory: "256Mi"
              cpu: "500m"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tls-certs
              mountPath: /tls
              readOnly: true
            - name: rotation-config
              mountPath: /config
        - name: tls-watcher
          image: your-tls-watcher:latest
          env:
            - name: TLS_PATH
              value: /tls
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tls-certs
              mountPath: /tls
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: tls-certs
          secret:
            secretName: api-tls-secret
        - name: rotation-config
          configMap:
            name: rotation-config
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: secure-api-pdb
  namespace: ssl
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure-api
```

## Verification Under Load
1. Apply the manifest and verify both pods are Running
2. Confirm the TLS certificate is mounted in /tls
3. Test readiness: curl http://localhost:8443/health
4. Test liveness: curl http://localhost:8443/ready
5. Simulate a pod failure: kubectl delete pod -n ssl -l app=secure-api
6. Verify the PDB allows disruption but maintains availability
7. Update rotation-config and observe rolling restart trigger

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills around in-cluster tooling, Pod security checks, and non-intrusive governance in a namespace-scoped pattern. It avoids admission webhooks and reinforces RBAC, Secrets, PVCs, InitContainers, and NetworkPolicies.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped Deployment pattern without admission controllers
- SecurityContext defaults: non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, runAsUser
- Secret-backed Bearer token for API calls and in-cluster service accounts
- Logs persisted to a PVC; InitContainer for curl/jq
- Readiness/Liveness probes and a strict egress policy via NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: compliance-guard
  namespace: your-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: compliance-guard
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: compliance-guard
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: init-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq > /dev/null 2>&1 || true"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
      containers:
        - name: guard
          image: your-registry/compliance-guard:latest
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: compliance-token
          env:
            - name: PORTAL_URL
              value: "http://compliance-portal:8080"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do ./guard --check-pod-security; sleep 60; done"]
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
        
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: logs-pvc
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
          spreadConstraintLabelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: compliance-guard
```

- How would you test locally for violations?
- How would you scale this across thousands of namespaces?

questions.explanation:
This question assesses CKAD-level ability to compose a batch job with initialization steps, configuration management, and access controls. It also evaluates understanding of idempotence and rollback planning.

**Key Concepts**
- CronJob scheduling and `concurrencyPolicy` for preventing concurrent runs
- InitContainer for dependency installation
- ConfigMap and Secret mounting patterns
- PVC usage across Job pods
- Readiness and Liveness probes for batch workloads
- NetworkPolicy for egress restrictions

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-migrate
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  schedule: "0 * * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  backoffLimit: 3
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: busybox
            command: ['sh', '-c', 'wget -O /usr/local/bin/yq ... && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq']
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          containers:
          - name: migrate
            image: curlimages/curl
            args: ['sh', '-c', 'yq -o=json /manifests/*.yaml > /out/manifests.json']
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ['test', '-f', '/out/manifests.json']
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
              periodSeconds: 30
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ['sh', '-c', 'ls /out']
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 60
            volumeMounts:
            - name: manifests
              mountPath: /manifests
            - name: out
              mountPath: /out
            - name: config
              mountPath: /config
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: credentials
          volumes:
          - name: manifests
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: manifest-pvc
          - name: out
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: manifest-pvc
          - name: config
            configMap:
              name: migrate-options
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

**Rollback Strategy**: To rollback, either suspend the CronJob with `kubectl patch cronjob data-migrate -n analytics -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'` or reduce the `successfulJobsHistoryLimit` to 0 to prevent new Jobs from being created.

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests knowledge of namespace-scoped governance primitives (LimitRange, ResourceQuota) and how defaults affect scheduling, QoS, and multi-tenant fairness in CKAD.

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses CKAD fundamentals, including CronJobs, PVCs, ConfigMaps, InitContainers, Secrets, TLS sidecars, probes, and NetworkPolicies within a realistic risk-based scenario.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and backoff management
- PVC-mounted configuration discovery
- YAML validation with yq for key extraction
- InitContainers for tool installation and sidecar patterns
- Secrets management and TLS certificate rotation
- Namespace-level network policy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: config-scan
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "0 0 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: yq-installer
            image: busybox:1.36
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              wget -O /usr/local/bin/yq https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.35.1/yq_linux_amd64
              chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
          containers:
          - name: scanner
            image: curlimages/curl:latest
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              for cm in $(kubectl get configmap -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
                kubectl get configmap $cm -o yaml | yq e '.data | keys' - | grep -v '^---\|config.json' && echo "$cm"
              done | curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d @- http://config-scan-portal:8080/api/v1/scan
            env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: config-scan-secret
                  key: api-key
            volumeMounts:
            - name: configs
              mountPath: /configs
          - name: tls-sidecar
            image: nginx:alpine
            ports:
            - containerPort: 443
              name: https
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /ready
                port: 443
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 443
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tls-certs
              mountPath: /etc/nginx/certs
              readOnly: true
          volumes:
          - name: configs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: config-scan-pvc
          - name: tmp
            emptyDir: {}
          - name: tls-certs
            secret:
              secretName: config-scan-tls
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: config-scan-pvc
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadOnlyMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: config-scan-secret
  namespace: target-namespace
type: Opaque
stringData:
  api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: config-scan-network-policy
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      job-name: config-scan
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: config-scan-portal
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **PVC vs ConfigMap listing**: Using a PVC requires storage provisioning but allows scanning ConfigMap YAML files directly. Listing ConfigMaps via kubectl is simpler but lacks filesystem semantics.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD ability to implement per-namespace GitOps, use InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, and NetworkPolicy; validates YAML tooling, apply flow, and status reporting.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace GitOps design patterns
- InitContainer provisioning and tool installation
- YAML validation with kubeval and yamllint
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for configuration
- PVC-based log streaming and persistence
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy for egress control
- Drift detection and status reporting via ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for a per-namespace GitOps runner
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gitops-runner
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gitops-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gitops-runner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: git-clone
        image: alpine/git:latest
        env:
        - name: REPO_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: repo-url
        - name: TARGET_PATH
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: target-path
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          apk add --no-cache git yq
          git clone $(REPO_URL) /workspace/repo
          cd /workspace/repo
          yq eval '.spec.path = "$(TARGET_PATH)"' . > manifests.yaml
      containers:
      - name: validator
        image: kubeval/kubeval:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          kubeval /workspace/manifests.yaml > /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          yamllint -d relaxed /workspace/manifests.yaml >> /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          kubectl apply -f /workspace/manifests.yaml --namespace=$(NAMESPACE)
          kubectl get -f /workspace/manifests.yaml -o jsonpath='{.status}' > /gitops-status
      volumes:
      - name: workspace
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: gitops-logs
```
